correctness.rationale: For N>=6, elementary probabilities for one, two and three specified disjoint matched pairs are 1/(N-1), 1/((N-1)(N-3)), and 1/((N-1)(N-3)(N-5)). Every parallel pair conflicts with exactly 2(d_i+d_j-3) potential loops; tallying all compatible six-stub configurations gives the exact mixed moment. Subtracting the exact mean product yields the stated rational covariance. Regular substitution reduces its sign to vd(2-d)+2d-3, positive for d=2 (v>=3), negative for every d>=3 (v>=2, vd even). The 4-stub exception is computed separately and asymptotic powers follow directly. A standalone checker independently enumerates small matchings and checks rational identities. No infinite step depends on finite checks.

value.rationale: The two canonical defects precisely characterize failure of simplicity in the configuration model. Known joint Poisson limits suppress finite-size dependence; the theorem establishes opposite correlation directions and different decay orders between the natural degree-two boundary and all higher regular degrees. The same exact identity covers arbitrary degree profiles, yielding useful finite corrections to defect dependence without asymptotic assumptions. This is a qualitative change, not a textbook restatement of defect expectations.
